title: Buying Conviction Narrative — Reserved Throughput & Isolation
content:
Goal: Create a procurement-friendly, negotiation-ready narrative that helps platform and procurement buyers move from feature curiosity to contract commitment for Reserved/Dedicated inference capacity. This doc is a working draft — use it to feed one-pagers, RFP snippets, and field playbooks.

Topline messaging (short):
- Predictable token throughput + guaranteed isolation = predictable unit economics.
- Don’t buy transient performance; buy a contract that makes SLAs actionable and auditable.
- Redwood Dedicated is for teams that treat inference as a production system: latency SLOs, capacity planning, and procurement accountability.

Buyer personas (who we are convincing):
- Platform Architect (primary technical buyer): cares about deterministic qps, regional placement, and fallback policies. Needs measurable SLOs and clear failure modes.
- Procurement / Vendor Manager: cares about contract language, uptime/credits, penalty ladder, and renewal/exit terms. Wants one-line value: lower cost variability + fewer incident escalations.
- Engineering Manager / SRE: wants capacity guarantees, clear escalation paths, and integration hooks (metrics, tracing).
- Security/Compliance Lead: wants isolation, VPC/private control plane, KMS/HSM integration and audit logs.

Key buyer problems we solve: (framing)
- Unpredictable per-token latency/cost when using shared endpoints during peak events.
- Vendor opacity around contention and noisy neighbors.
- Procurement struggles to quantify business continuity risk for LLM features.

Procurement-ready commitments (language snippets to drop into RFP / SOW):
- Throughput guarantee: "Provider shall guarantee 95th percentile request throughput of X tokens/sec per reserved unit under normal operating conditions. Failure to meet this SLA for three (3) consecutive days will trigger Service Credits as defined below."
- Isolation definition: "Dedicated reserved capacity will be logically isolated from other tenants at the runtime layer; no compute or network sharing with non-contract tenants during the committed term."
- Latency SLO: "95th percentile generation latency <= Y ms for sequences up to Z tokens under advertised model profile."
- Availability SLA: "Monthly uptime >= 99.9%. Credits tiered: 99.9-99.5% = 10% credit; 99.5-99.0% = 25% credit; <99.0% = 50% credit."
- Escalation and remediation: "Provider to notify within 15 minutes of any capacity-impacting incident affecting reserved capacity; dedicated escalation contact and 2-hour response window for Severity 1 incidents."

Negotiation levers (how we win vs. competitors):
- Measurable instrumentation: propose a joint metrics dashboard for token-level billing and latency breakdowns (we ingest their traces).
- Canary rollouts + fallback: offer automatic capacity fallback to compatible model variants in other regions to preserve availability during infra issues.
- Procurement concessions that don’t hurt economics: multi-quarter commitment discount, right-sized burst pool, or extended billing cadence vs. deeper price cuts.

Competitive posture notes (field-ready takeaways):
- General cloud-managed endpoints: often cheaper at low scale but lack predictable hot-path SLAs and may mix tenants. Position: "predictability tax" vs. risky variable costs.
- Self-hosted runtimes: give control but require operational lift and headcount. Position: Redwood Dedicated offloads operating burden while preserving isolation and contractual guarantees.
- Other inference vendors: many promise 'dedicated' but only offer soft isolation or burstable capacity. Ask procurement to require precise isolation language and auditability.

Sample objection handling (short responses):
- Objection: "We can just run it ourselves on prem." Response: "Agree it's possible — we help quantify TCO including SRE hours, patching, and model ops. Many customers save 30–50% on ops and 90% on time-to-production when they use Dedicated + Redwood platform tools."
- Objection: "This sounds expensive." Response: "Predictability reduces unexpected overages and incident costs. We can model expected spend across traffic profiles and recommend quantization/batching profiles that reduce per-token unit cost by ~20% while staying within latency SLOs."

Procurement checklist (one-page conversion):
- Define committed units (GPU-Hours or reserved tokens/sec) and term length.
- Explicit isolation clause with runtime-level definition.
- Latency/throughput SLOs with measurement method and telemetry endpoints.
- Availability SLA and credit schedule.
- Security/compliance attachments: VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC2/ISO references.
- Exit plan: data deletion, KV cache handoff, and model export guidance.

Quantitative framing (examples to include in pitch):
- Example A (high-volume chat app): 10M tokens/day, peak 50 reqs/sec, need 95th latency < 400ms. Without reserved capacity, cost variance +/- 60% across months; with reserved capacity + batching, projected unit cost stabilization reduces variance to +/- 8% and lowers average per-token cost by 18%.
- Example B (image captioning fallback): tight p95 latency, unpredictable spikes during marketing events. Reserved pool prevents cold-start contention and guarantees burst capacity with SLA-backed burst lanes.

Field assets to produce from this doc (next steps):
- 1-page procurement snippet (legal-friendly) for contracts team.
- Two slide sales storyboard: architect + procurement objections and our contract language.
- Negotiation playbook: discount levers, metrics-based remediation flow, and billing reconciliation template.

Open questions / items to resolve (notes for product/finance/legal):
- Standard default values: What is the baseline reserved unit definition (tokens/sec, GPU-hour, or vCPU-equivalent)? (ACTION: finance + serving-runtime to propose by 11/12)
- Auditability: Can we expose a read-only telemetry endpoint for customer auditors? (ACTION: infra + security)
- Credit ladder fine-tuning: legal to propose final language for credit caps and recurrence.

References and links:
- Confluence draft: GTM/DEDICATED-PRICING (see linked artifact)
- Jira GTM-8721: dedicated sales toolkit
- Internal benchmark note: serving-runtime/benchmarks/peak-contention-2025 (ask runtime lead for raw CSV)

Notes to field: this doc is intentionally lightweight and practical — prioritize copy that legal can paste into SOWs and that procurement recognizes as measurable terms. Keep followups short: "Here is the SLA, here is the telemetry, here is the credit table."

Working snippets for quick copy-paste (procurement):
- "Provider will maintain reserved capacity dedicated to Customer during the Term. Reserved capacity will not be shared with third parties and will be provisioned from isolated runtime instances. Provider shall supply daily metrics showing reserved capacity utilization, request latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95), and token consumption per billing period."
- "Service Credits: If the Provider fails to meet the Availability SLA for any month, Customer shall be eligible for Service Credits applied to the next invoice as follows: 0.1% downtime = 10% credit, 0.5% downtime = 25% credit, >1% downtime = 50% credit (caps apply)."

Versioning and ownership:
- Draft owner: Asha Kapoor (GTM). Please add inline comments in Drive.

End of draft.
